newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan-China trade rises 2.6 pct in Jan-Oct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan-China trade rises 2.6 pct in Jan-Oct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's indirect trade with China rose 2.6 percent to US$17.76 billion in the first 10 months of 1996 from the same period in 1995, the Board of Foreign Trade said in a statement on Saturday.
Taiwan's exports to China grew 3.9 percent to $15.253 billion from a year earlier, while imports slid 4.5 percent to $2.508 billion, the statement said.
In October, exports to China rose 8.7 percent to $1.633 billion from a year ago while imports increased 0.9 percent to $270 million.
During the January-October period, Taiwan enjoyed a trade surplus of $12.746 billion with China, up a year-on-year 5.7 percent, the board said.

Beijing, which considers Taiwan a renegade province, held war games near the Taiwan Strait ahead of the island's presidential election on March 23 to warn voters not to drop a pledge to reunify with China.
Officials have said the war games made Taiwanese businessmen less willing to invest in the mainland.
Taiwan bans direct contact with China. All trade must be conducted through a third region, mostly Hong Kong. Some 30,000 Taiwan firms have invested more than $20 billion in China.
